slides.0.title: The wine regions
slides.0.subtitle: How INAVI describes the country's regions
slides.1.title: Three southern regions
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Metropolitana
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Canelones, Montevideo and San José. INAVI says it holds over 70% of the wineries. Montevideo has the oldest vineyards, and the city's growth pushed growers into Canelones
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Oceánica
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Maldonado and Rocha. Atlantic influence, higher ground and the most varied geology. Around Laguna Garzón there are gravel and alluvial soils, and INAVI puts the crystalline basement at about 2.5 billion years old
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Litoral Sur
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Colonia, Soriano and Río Negro. The warm waters of the Uruguay and Paraná rivers keep the climate mild. The oldest winery is in Colonia, and the Carmelo area is singled out
slides.1.content: The three southern regions hold the great majority of vines.
slides.2.title: The north and the interior
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Litoral Norte
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Salto, Paysandú and Artigas. About 50–60 m above sea level, hot, with wide temperature swings; INAVI says Salto reaches 40° by day and 20° at night. Harriague worked in Salto
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Norte
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Rivera and Tacuarembó. Vineyards on sandstone. Some at Cerro Chapeu in Rivera sit at 220 m on deep, free-draining red sand, in a climate like Brazil's Campanha
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Central and Centro-Este
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Central is Durazno, Florida and Lavalleja; Centro-Este is Lavalleja and Treinta y Tres. INAVI's page says "six regions" but lists seven, and Lavalleja appears in both
slides.2.content: Even official websites can be inconsistent; note it when you see it.
slides.3.title: The regions in numbers
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Metropolitana dominates
slides.3.highlights.0.content: On the 2025 report, Canelones, Montevideo and San José together hold about 83% of the national area
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Maldonado third
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Maldonado has 7.39%, behind Montevideo; Rocha, also in Oceánica, has only 0.33%
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Figures that disagree
slides.3.highlights.2.content: INAVI's regions page says Canelones makes "60% of production"; the 2025 report gives 73.87%. The years and methods differ
slides.3.content: Each northern department has under 2% of the area, yet the history began there.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Which region are Maldonado and Rocha in?
The region most shaped by the Atlantic.
Which department is Cerro Chapeu in?
It is in the Norte region.
